incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident 2025-07-21T03:12Z — latency-regression detected for /v1/generate (p95 spike). Paging oncall Maya (oncall)

Maya (oncall): saw the page, checking dashboards now. p50 looks ok but p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.4s at 03:10Z.

Alex (support): customers X and Y reported timeouts around 03:12Z, high error rate in proxy (504s). Not sure if it's the same cluster.

Maya (oncall): assigning. @Javier can you join? putting an incident channel here.

Javier (eng-runtime): I'm in. first checks: no config rollouts in the last 24h according to deploy-bot.

Priya (SRE): I see a jump in kernel sched wait on the GPU hosts around 03:09Z. Attaching perf counters snapshot shortly.

Maya (oncall): Timeline so far: 02:58Z normal, 03:09Z p95 increases, 03:12Z customer reports. Need quick mitigation if high impact.

Evan (eng-platform): Can we fall back routing to the lower-latency model variant in the same region? Canary policy exists.

Javier (eng-runtime): We can flip routing to model-gnome-small (compatible) in 2 min. That reduces token cost but will lower throughput to single-gpu pods for some customers.

Maya (oncall): Do it. Evan/Javier coordinate. Mark mitigation: partial routing change.

Evan (eng-platform): rolling routing change started. API header X-Model-Override: model-gnome-small. Will monitor p95.

incident-bot: mitigation "partial-routing-to-model-gnome-small" started by Evan at 03:18Z.

Alex (support): Notifying affected customers: sent temp status message to customer X.

Priya (SRE): logs I'm seeing from 03:08-03:11: many requests experiencing long kernel scheduling latencies. snippet: ```
/var/log/inference/gpu_sched.log 03:09:47 WARN queue_wait_us=120000 cpu_wait_us=98000
/var/log/inference/gpu_sched.log 03:09:52 WARN queue_wait_us=135000 cpu_wait_us=110000
```

Javier (eng-runtime): Can someone paste a perf top or trace span? I'm trying to see if it's a runtime scheduling artifact or a kernel change.

Priya (SRE): perf counters (aggregate across hosts): ```
Timestamp: 2025-07-21T03:09Z
context-switches: +34%
softirqs: +8%
cpu-cycles: -2%
cache-misses: +60%
sched-wait-ns(avg): 110000
```

Javier (eng-runtime): interesting — cache-misses up. Could be PCIe congestion or driver change. Any infra changes noted?

Evan (eng-platform): No driver or kernel upgrades on schedule. But auto-update bundle for node images ran at 02:46Z on a few canary nodes (non-prod) — not the prod pool. I will double-check.

Maya (oncall): Who can run a full trace span for a slow request? Need the span IDs and logs.

Priya (SRE): Pasting a sampled trace (sanitized): ```
span_id: 0x7f2a
root -> runtime.dispatch (120ms) -> runtime.kv_cache_lookup (30ms) -> runtime.kernel_queue_wait (1150ms) -> gpu.infer (45ms)
```

Javier (eng-runtime): kernel_queue_wait of ~1.15s matches p95. That suggests the runtime is blocked waiting to be scheduled on GPU. Could be long-running background copy or a blocked process.

Evan (eng-platform): I'm seeing elevated i/o wait on NVMe on those hosts at exactly the same time window. ```
ssh ops@host-03 'iostat -x 1 3' -> avg await=25ms -> spike at 03:09 to await=350ms across multiple NVMe devices
```

Maya (oncall): Hypotheses (thread):
- H1: sudden NVMe/io congestion causing kernel scheduling delays for GPU tasks (supported by iostat + cache-miss increase).
- H2: noisy neighbor job spawned heavy CPU/io (check crons / batch jobs).
- H3: regression in kernel driver or runtime causing longer queue waits (less evidence currently).

Javier (eng-runtime): I'll pull container metrics and check if any big memcpys or host-level processes were active. Also dumping RT priority threads.

Priya (SRE): On affected hosts, I see a cron job for snapshot backups starting at 03:06Z on two hosts — backups involve tar + compression to local disk, possible contention. Logs: ```
/var/log/cron 03:06:05 backup-snapshot.sh start
/var/log/backup 03:06:10 tar ... | gzip -9 ... -> heavy CPU + IO
```

Evan (eng-platform): That matches H2. Were backup jobs supposed to be zoned to maintenance pool? Looks like scheduling bug drifted to prod nodes. I'm scoping the rollout of backup scheduling changes.

Maya (oncall): Immediate actions:
- Evan: block backup cron on prod hosts (temp) -> actioned?
- Javier: keep routing fallback to model-gnome-small for 15m, monitor p95
- Priya: collect full perf samples and kernel logs for RCA

Evan (eng-platform): blocked the cron via salt on prod hosts at 03:22Z. Confirmed no new backup starts.

incident-bot: mitigation "block-prod-backup-cron" executed by Evan at 03:22Z.

Maya (oncall): p95 down to ~320ms at 03:25Z after blocking backups + routing change. Still above baseline but much better.

Alex (support): customers X and Y acknowledged improvement. Updating status page: "latency improved after mitigation, engineering investigating root cause".

Javier (eng-runtime): Full trace post-mitigation: ```
span_id: 0x8a3f
root -> runtime.dispatch (90ms) -> runtime.kv_cache_lookup (25ms) -> runtime.kernel_queue_wait (180ms) -> gpu.infer (40ms)
```

Priya (SRE): attaching perf counter full dump (pasted): ```
Before 03:09: sched-wait-ns(avg)=110000, cache-misses=+60%
After 03:25: sched-wait-ns(avg)=17000, cache-misses=+8%
```

Maya (oncall): Good. Let's capture a concise incident note for follow-up:
- Impact: Elevated p95 latency for /v1/generate causing timeouts for a subset of customers between 03:09-03:25Z.
- Short-term mitigations: blocked mis-scheduled backup cron on prod hosts; partial routing fallback to model-gnome-small.
- Probable root cause: backup cron jobs ran on prod GPU nodes causing NVMe/CPU contention and long kernel queue waits -> increased kernel_queue_wait spans in runtime -> p95 spike.
- Evidence: cron logs + iostat spikes + perf counters + trace spans.

Javier (eng-runtime): Postmortem action items:
- enforce scheduling constraints for backup jobs (Evan)
- add early detection rule for kernel_queue_wait span > 500ms (Javier)
- track and alert NVMe await spikes across GPU pool (Priya)

Evan (eng-platform): I'll open a change to re-scoped scheduled jobs and add node affinity for backups. ETA for complete fix: 48h.

Maya (oncall): Oncall handoff: I'll write the incident summary and hand to daytime SRE at 07:00Z. Full RCA doc to be created in the incidents tracker.

Alex (support): I'll follow up with customers with a post-incident note and include mitigation timeline.

incident-bot: Incident 1798887776 mitigations recorded: partial-routing-to-model-gnome-small, block-prod-backup-cron. Status: mitigated at 03:25Z.

Maya (oncall): thanks team. closing this channel for live mitigation — please continue RCA in the incident doc and paste final artifacts there.

Evan (eng-platform): adding links to logs and perf dumps in the incident doc: s3://redwood-incidents/1798887776/perf-dumps.tar.gz

Priya (SRE): leaving final note: observed kernel_queue_wait signature might be useful for future automated triage.

Javier (eng-runtime): +1. Will prototype a zap rule to flag that span profile.

Maya (oncall): handoff complete.
